title: The Financial Time Machine — Amiga source recovery and SDL reconstruction

notes: This repository preserves and adapts the 1985 Amiga The Financial Time Machine source release after loss of lessee6.c. The November 2014 README explicitly describes reconstructing missing functionality and replacing the backend for modern systems. ftm.c retains the financial-game model, stock/timeline logic, player portfolios, command handling and save/load behavior with local SDL-backed drawing/input replacements. The historical 1982 Odyssey 2 and later C64 editions are mentioned as ancestry only; this repository's actual source basis is the Amiga C release, so they are not additional source-platform records. This is a game subject with original-source restoration, reconstruction of missing source functions and an SDL/API reimplementation. It is neither a binary decompilation nor a claim that the lost source has been recovered completely. Modern ftm.c is derived from the original C and adds replacement RastPort-style graphics/input behavior. The latest commit imports a recovered validity_check chunk as validity_check_original but explicitly says it is not used yet. The current parser remains a separate replacement. The 2014 reconstruction date is explicit in README and commit history; 1985 denotes the original release, not the reconstruction start. README documents a C99 compiler, SDL and make; Makefile compiles the C files and links -lSDL, and no build/run was attempted. ftm.c explicitly defines warning-returning STUB bodies for calc_taxes, earnings_display, click, add_purchase and del_purchase. The active validity_check can emit UNHANDLED COMMAND GIVEN; the recovered validity_check_original is not the active implementation. A net-worth FIXME is also retained. These defects prevent any claim of complete restored gameplay. All four build flags remain null: neither a recipe, a large source file nor the recovered historical fragment verifies compilation, runtime, playability or binary identity. The preserved original is an Amiga game, while the modern output is an SDL/POSIX adaptation represented under Linux. This is a source-based host adaptation, not a bundled 68k emulator or a newly verified native-Amiga release. The README gives library/build prerequisites rather than a hardware minimum; no host ISA, RAM or OS-version floor is established. Financial-game commands remain incomplete regardless of whether a window could be opened. The Linux label describes the POSIX-oriented adaptation and does not certify builds across Linux architectures or distributions. One record covers the lost-file recovery, original C preservation and SDL adaptation, rather than counting each as a new game. The latest commit attributes a recovered validity_check fragment to Crashdisk's EAB post and preserves its incomplete/unused status; README links the broader Amiga recovery discussion. The original Odyssey 2/C64 ancestry is context, not a separately inspected code lineage in this batch. No root project-level LICENSE/COPYING grant was found in the complete tree or reviewed README. Original shipment with C source is not itself a modern redistribution grant; rights remain unresolved, and no unrestricted redistribution conclusion is recorded. The modern implementation uses SDL with POSIX headers and timing/input functions; the Makefile links -lSDL with an ordinary C compiler. These sources do not establish a host ISA matrix or exact processor requirement. target_cpu therefore remains empty even though Linux/POSIX is the identified build family. Portable C99, unistd.h, sys/time.h and an SDL dependency do not prove x86-64/ARM support. The historical Amiga origin also does not establish that this modernized tree still rebuilds as a native Amiga executable.

Build: The archive includes assembly modules, include directives, fixed origins, level data, graphics and disk routines. BOOT.S ends with a historical SAV directive; no turnkey modern build script exists in the inspected complete tree. Toolchain and disk-layout reconstruction would still need to be established. Limitations: Static discovery only. No source was built, executed, played, hardware-tested or byte-compared; independent verification flags remain null. Runtime profiles: BOOT.S calls check128k, checks the IIe/IIc/GS identity and auxiliary-memory behavior, and displays a 128 KB IIc/IIe requirement on failure.
